claims.text: A screening method can integrate machine-learning-calibrated CALPHAD calculations with atomic-mass variance, atomic-size mismatch, and local lattice distortion descriptors.
The integrated method will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity HEAs more accurately than conventional empirical or isolated thermodynamic models.
Single-phase HEA solid solutions inherently exhibit lattice distortions because they contain multiple principal elements.
High atomic-mass variance enhances phonon scattering in HEAs.
Large atomic-size differences enhance phonon scattering in HEAs.
The target single-phase HEA microstructure can be retained from 50 °C to 900 °C under relevant synthesis and testing conditions.
Local lattice distortions induced by compositional complexity act as phonon-scattering centers.
Mass fluctuations induced by compositional complexity act as phonon-scattering centers.
Enhanced configurational entropy combined with controlled atomic-size and mass differences increases phonon-scattering efficiency.
Capturing the interactions among entropy, size mismatch, mass variance, and lattice distortion enables the model to identify alloys with reduced phonon thermal conductivity.
HEAs selected by the approach will have thermal conductivity between 10 and 17 W/(m·K).
HEAs selected by the approach will have thermal conductivity approximately 20% lower than values predicted or achieved through conventional selection methods.
HEAs selected by the approach will maintain phase stability at high temperatures.
Existing empirical or CALPHAD-based predictions lacking machine-learning phonon-scattering descriptors typically overestimate HEA thermal conductivity.
Existing models lack precise correlation with atomic-scale disorder.
The approach is expected to be most effective for single-phase HEAs with pronounced atomic-mass and atomic-size variation.
The approach may be less accurate for multiphase alloys or alloys with minimal atomic variance.
Experimental datasets on phonon transport in HEAs are limited.
